title: ASENA narcotics analysis software flags a car at the Köy Hizmetleri checkpoint in Şırnak; the dog Hector finds 86.6 kg of skunk in 119 packages and three lawyers are remanded
summary: Şırnak police stopped a car selected by the ASENA narcotics analysis software; the dog Hector found 86.6 kg of skunk in 119 packages in the trunk, and three lawyers were remanded (March 2025).
account: Şırnak Provincial Police stopped a vehicle at the Köy Hizmetleri (Village Services) police checkpoint after ASENA, which DHA describes as police software 'in artificial intelligence format', selected it for inspection; the narcotics dog Hector then found 86 kilograms 600 grams of skunk in 119 packages hidden in the trunk, and three occupants, M.E., H.K. and Ş.A., were detained (Sözcü/DHA and Habertürk/DHA, March 17, 2025). Diken, citing İHA, gives ASENA's full name as Analiz Sistemleri Narkotik Ağı (Narcotics Analysis Systems Network) and says the three were lawyers registered with the Mardin Bar Association who were taken to court after police processing and remanded in custody (Diken, March 18, 2025). None of the reports gives the day of the stop, what data ASENA analyzed or how it chose the car, or any official's name; the first report date is used here.
purpose: Police analysis software built to pick out vehicles and people likely to be carrying narcotics for checkpoint stops; this seizure was that use.
system: ASENA (Analiz Sistemleri Narkotik Ağı), Turkish police narcotics analysis software
deployer: Şırnak Provincial Police Directorate (Turkish National Police)

ratings.reason: 86.6 kg of skunk was taken out of circulation and three suspects remanded; a measurable interdiction result, but the reports specify no downstream harm averted.
The Şırnak police turned a software flag into a large seizure and three remands, per the DHA and İHA reports; a measurable result for the unit.

ai_role.statement: ASENA supplied the selection and nothing more: DHA's wording is that the vehicle was identified and stopped 'thanks to the ASENA software', after which the dog Hector found the packages and officers made the arrests. No report describes ASENA's inputs, its ranking method, or whether an analyst reviewed the flag before the stop.
